title: User Validation Errors
prompt: A TypeScript form for users requires a non-empty name and at least one selected tag. Write a function that returns validation error messages for missing fields.

explanation.beginner:
Example: userValidationErrors({"name":"Alpha","tags":["one"]}) produces []. Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Compare “reports both errors”: input [{"name":" ","tags":[]}] produces ["Name is required","Choose at least one tag"]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Tempting mistake: Returning at the first error may hide other errors when the contract asks for all of them. Whitespace and empty strings need explicit treatment.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “reports both errors”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
